finding.claim: DELETE /reports/:id removes the report even when the authorize check denies access, because authorize() is called without await and its 403 rejection is never observed.
finding.source: Any HTTP DELETE to /reports/:id from a session whose user lacks the 'delete' grant on the target report (req.params.id, req.user from session).

trace.note: authorize(...) called without await; runs to await db.grants then returns pending promise, handler continues
403 throw occurs inside the unobserved promise
remove executes before denial is known

finding.guards_checked: authorize() itself throws on missing grant (lines 9-16) but its result is discarded; no try/catch or .catch; no await at call site; session middleware (lines 4-7) only copies req.user and enforces nothing. Decoys 25-28 do not match. Additional impact: unhandled rejection can crash the Node process on Node 15+ defaults.

verdict.guard_found: None effective. authorize() (server.js:9-16) does throw a 403 on a missing grant at lines 11-14, but the call at server.js:20 is a bare statement with no await, no try/catch, and no .catch, so the rejection is never observed. The delete at server.js:21 runs as soon as authorize() suspends at its await on line 10. The session middleware (server.js:4-7) only copies req.user and enforces nothing.
verdict.reason: server.js:20 calls authorize() without await, so the 403 thrown at server.js:14 becomes an unobserved rejection and db.reports.remove runs at server.js:21 regardless of the grant check. The attacker needs only a session whose user lacks the 'delete' grant on the target report, which is a low-privilege authenticated user. The trace has one imprecise line reference: the throw is at line 14, not line 11 (line 11 is the if-check), which does not change the result.

finding.claim: PUT /reports/:id passes the entire client request body into db.reports.update, so a writer can set arbitrary record fields (ownership, tenant, grants, or id) via mass assignment.
finding.source: req.body (JSON parsed by express.json at server.js:3); attacker must hold a legitimate 'write' grant on the report.

trace.note: authorize 'write' is awaited, so the grant gates the write
whole req.body written to record with no field allow-list

finding.guards_checked: Grant check is correctly awaited and applied to the same record being updated. No allow-list, no stripping of server-owned keys, no check on id/owner/tenant fields. Impact depends on db.reports schema, which is not in the repo; medium confidence.

verdict.guard_found: authorize(user, "write", report) at server.js:27 is awaited and throws a 403 when the grant is missing (server.js:9-16), so only callers holding a 'write' grant on this report reach line 28. No field allow-list, server-owned-key stripping, or id/owner/tenant check exists between lines 26 and 28. The db.reports.update implementation is not in the repo, so any filtering there cannot be seen.
verdict.reason: The trace at server.js:25-28 is accurate and the write grant at server.js:27 is awaited and enforced, but req.body is passed unfiltered to db.reports.update at server.js:28 with no allow-list. Whether that is a real escalation depends on whether the report record has owner, tenant, or grant fields and on the unseen db layer, so it cannot be decided from this repo. Separately, server.js:20 calls authorize without await, so the delete route's 403 becomes an unhandled rejection and db.reports.remove at server.js:21 still runs; that is a different and more serious auth bypass than F2.

finding.claim: Unauthorized PUT /reports/:id rejects inside an async handler with no catch, producing an unhandled promise rejection that can crash the process (Express 4) or hang the request.
finding.source: Request to PUT /reports/:id from a user without 'write' grant on the report, or a request with no req.user.
finding.sink: Unhandled promise rejection from await authorize(...) at server.js:27 (availability impact)

trace.note: await authorize rejects with 403 error when grant missing
async handler has no try/catch and Express 4 does not forward rejections to next

finding.guards_checked: await is present and correct; no try/catch or error middleware in this file. Express version unknown because package manifest is not in the directory; conditional finding, lower severity.

verdict.guard_found: none. authorize() (server.js:9-16) throws a 403 rather than returning a bool, and the PUT handler (server.js:25-30) awaits it at line 27 with no try/catch. No error-handling middleware is registered (server.js:32 is only app.listen). The guard that exists (grants check at lines 10-15) is the one that throws, so the rejection is what reaches the handler.
verdict.reason: At server.js:27 the await on authorize() rejects with a 403 for any user lacking a "write" grant, and the async handler at server.js:25 has no catch. Under Express 4 (the version the finding assumes; the manifest is absent so Express 5 cannot be ruled out here) that rejection is not forwarded to next(), so it becomes an unhandled rejection that crashes Node 15+ by default, or leaves the request unanswered. The finding holds only on Express 4; on Express 5 the rejection would reach the default error handler and return a 403 instead.
